Following the ongoing 25% discount on AirPods Pro 3 and last week's $120 off AirPods Max 2, today's 9to5Toys lunch hour headline sees Amazon once again dropping the AirTag 2 to an all-new historic low, with the 4-pack now selling for $80 (that's $20 each). We also have Apple's 24GB/1TB M5 MacBook Pro down $320, plus this 2TB M5 Pro for $500 off, and don't miss the all-time low $25 on Anker's new SmartTrack Find My wallet card at Amazon, as well as LG's 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 display at a massive $2,200 below the Apple Studio Display XDR (all-time low). Read on for details.

Latest AirPods Pro 3 maintains 25% discount, next generation widely expected to arrive in 2027

  • AirPods Pro 3 $190 (originally $249)
  • AirPods Max 2 $429 (originally $549)
  • AirPods 4 $99 (originally $129)

Wow! AirTag 2 discounted again, 4-pack now at all-time low $80 (that's $20 each)

Here we go folks! Amazon has just posted an all-time low on the Apple 2026 AirTag 2 4-pack — just $20 per tracker.

Amazon now has the AirTag 2 4-pack down to $79.99 with free shipping.

We've been tracking this official pack at $89.99 all last week, then Amazon cut it to $85 yesterday, and now a fresh week brings another step down. Priced at $99, you're looking at roughly 20% off, which doesn't sound like a lot, but it's a pretty notable discount for the latest AirTag 2.

This pack works out to about $20 per AirTag on average, the lowest price we've seen since its launch earlier this year.

The single AirTag 2 link is still holding at last week's $24 Prime-shipped low, but the 4-pack has dropped even lower (again).

The $20-per-tag price here matches the best open-box pricing we saw at Best Buy last week, just for reference.

Apple's 24GB/1TB M5 MacBook Pro now down $320, 2TB M5 Pro discounted $500

Beyond the ongoing 25% discount on AirPods Pro 3 and the AirTag 2 hitting its tracked low, we're rolling into a new week with a few notable deals on the latest MacBook Pro lineup. Amazon still has the 2TB M5 Pro down $500, and we've also just spotted a much more affordable M5 MacBook Pro 24GB configuration down $300. Details below.

If you've got your eye on the more powerful M5 Pro, Amazon's $500-off model is absolutely worth a look. But if the cheaper M5 is more your speed, B&H's 14-inch 24GB/1TB configuration is quite compelling:

B&H has once again slashed the 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro with 24GB RAM and 1TB of internal storage down to $1,899 with free shipping.

  • 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro 24GB/1TB $1,899 (originally $2,219)
  • Includes upgraded 96W Apple charger

On this $2,199-configured machine, B&H is also throwing in the official 96W Apple charger — which would cost you an extra $20 if configured at Apple's own site.

Amazon currently has the same MacBook Pro configuration for $2,049, but it ships with the standard 70W charger.

All things considered, B&H's deal saves you $320, in line with previously mentioned offers, and comes in well below Amazon's current price.

However, as mentioned earlier, Amazon still has a notable markdown on the 14-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro 24GB/2TB, down to $2,699 — $500 off the $3,199 sticker price, and this deal likely won't last long.

Anker's new SmartTrack Find My wallet card (supports iOS or Android) hits all-time low $25 at Amazon

Anker recently launched a brand-new SmartTrack Find My wallet card — the first product to support both Apple's tracking platform and Google Find Hub — and it's now down to an all-time low $25 with Prime shipping at Amazon.

This product only debuted on Amazon last month at $35, saw a minor $5 trim by month's end, and now sees its first notable markdown for an all-time Amazon low.

That's nearly 30% off, matching the best deals we've tracked on other wallet tracker cards this year.

I'm personally a huge fan of the Nomad Tracking Cards — the standard version starts at $35, while the Pro with 16-month battery life goes for $45 — but regardless of which you choose, I think everyone should keep one in their wallet or cardholder. I never leave the house without mine.

Anker's latest SmartTrack Card E40 covers all the most important bases, including wireless charging, while supporting either Apple's Find My platform or Google Find Hub. At just 1.7mm thin with an alert volume of up to 80dB for finding it nearby — of course you can also just add it to the Find My and Find Hub apps to see its location on a map.

Organize your desk with Anker's clever power strip, now down to $58

LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 display hits lowest price, a whopping $2,200 below the Studio Display XDR

We just spotted a deal at B&H that drops the LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K display to $1,099.99 with free shipping. This display normally runs $2,000, and had peaked at around $1,597 in recent months. Today's offer matches the all-time low that Amazon first hit earlier this month, and that price is still live. LG's own site is also matching the $1,100 price today, so if one retailer sells out, you have plenty of options. The UltraFine evo 6K at this price is also substantially below Apple's displays. The Studio Display XDR starts at $3,299, meaning LG's 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 display is over $2,200 less. Even the standard Studio Display starts at $1,549, so you'd save roughly $500 and get a larger 32-inch 6K screen to boot. Read on for details.

The LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K is a high-end workstation display aimed at creators who want a large, sharp screen without upgrading to Apple's pricier options. Its 6144 x 3456 screen packs over 21 million pixels at 224 PPI, providing plenty of room for editing timelines, full-resolution content, tools, and multiple windows. Color coverage hits 99.5% Adobe RGB and supports VESA DisplayHDR 600 for better highlights and contrast. Connectivity is also comprehensive, including Thunderbolt 5, DisplayPort 2.1, HDMI, and USB-C. Mac users can also access calibrated color presets via LG's Studio Mode for more consistent creative work. All told, this 6K display is feature-rich for anyone who wants true large-screen real estate without paying Apple's display prices.

If you don't want to spend over $1,000 on a new display, Woot also has several more affordable Samsung workstation monitor deals. The M-series and other budget-friendly models are marked down, with entry-level prices starting at just $118.

Today's accessories and charging deals:

  • This ultra-thin UGREEN wallet tracker supports iPhone and Android, now down to just $20 (all-time low)
  • This compact UGREEN ultra-thin 45W Nexode Air charger is the thinnest in my EDC, now on sale for $27
  • Twelve South's AirFly Pro wireless audio transmitter slashed to $40 at Amazon (black or white)
  • Chipolo's Google Find Hub wallet card with action button/remote camera shutter, now $33
  • UGREEN's MagFlow 25W Qi2.2 car charger back up to $28 (originally $40)
  • Acer metal MagSafe golf cart holder slashed to $20 with Prime shipping

Latest wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro hits all-time low at Amazon, nearly 30% off (wired version also on sale)

As part of an end-of-summer string of discounts on Fire tablets, Fire TVs, and Blink smart home products, Amazon is now offering the all-time lowest price on the latest wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro, and bringing back the Prime Day all-time low on the wired model — both at nearly 30% off retail.

  • Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (originally $250)
  • Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (originally $250)

Although Ring has since launched the more affordably-priced Ring Peephole Cam 2K at $100, today we're focusing on several particularly notable deals on its newest Pro-series 4K models.

The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro has now returned to its Prime Day all-time low, appearing for the first time since promotions at the end of June. In fact, this is only the second time we've tracked this model below $200.

The wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro is now seeing its first markdown, also hitting an all-time low of $180.

As seen above, both models carry a $250 sticker price, so you're looking at nearly 30% off — the best deals we've found and the lowest prices seen to date.

The two are largely the same, featuring Retinal 4K imaging with up to 10x enhanced zoom, night vision, and a wide-angle view to better keep an eye on your doorstep; the wireless model comes with a Quick Release Ultra battery pack for easy charging and a notably simpler installation (no wiring required), while the wired model offers "uninterrupted power, uninterrupted protection."

For more details, check out our launch coverage from last September.

Best Buy launches new tech deals, NFL Sunday Ticket promotion, preseason TV deals

Amazon now takes $120 off all five colors of AirPods Max 2 (one of the best prices ever)

This week's big 60th anniversary sale event brings one of the best prices yet for Apple's 2026 AirPods Max 2, with Amazon now taking $120 off across all five colors.

Amazon has now dropped Apple's AirPods Max 2 to $429 with free shipping.

Priced the same as the previous generation at $549, you're looking at a solid $120 in savings — the best price available in brand-new condition from reputable retailers right now.

Best Buy has the Midnight black version down to $403.99 with free shipping in "excellent" open-box condition, which is lower, but the savings aren't substantial enough to warrant giving up a brand-new unit for such a small difference.

Apple released a true next-generation AirPods Max this year, unlike the previous iteration which simply got new colors and a USB-C port. Unlike the in-ear AirPods lineup, its over-ear line won't be updated at next month's new product announcement, so this week we can consider grabbing what might be the latest and greatest Apple over-ear headphones for a good while at $120 off.

Only one previous promotion has been cheaper than this one — the Prime Day earlier this year, which was $30 less than today's deal price — but stock was very unstable during that 4-day promotion.

Amazon selling this 512GB iPad mini at new low with $450 off (Renewed Premium)

Although iPad Air deals are just starting to pop up this week, iPad discounts overall have been weak or nearly nonexistent recently. However, we just spotted Amazon selling the 512GB iPad mini at a new low with a massive $450 off in top-quality Renewed Premium condition.

Amazon has now dropped the 512GB iPad mini A17 — the latest model — to $449 with free shipping.

That means this iPad, priced at $899 new from Apple, can now be purchased directly from Amazon for $450 less.

Worth noting: even before the price hike, we'd never seen this model go below $679 in new condition at Amazon.

As a reminder, Amazon Renewed Premium units aren't the same as regular Renewed items, nor even "excellent" condition refurbished units. Here's their standard:

  • Screen: If equipped with a screen, no scratches whatsoever.
  • Body: No visible cosmetic damage (scratches, dents, etc.) when viewed from 12 inches away.
  • Battery: If included, battery capacity exceeds 90% of original battery life.
  • Accessories: Original or generic accessories and packaging provided.
  • Guarantee: Renewed Premium items come with a 365-day return policy.

Amazon's top-quality Premium Renewed iPhone 17 Pro devices now $220 off (matches Prime Day deals)

While the official Apple Certified Refurbished Store is my first choice for iPhone deals, Apple still isn't selling the latest iPhone 17 Pro models there — looks like we'll have to wait until after the 18 series launches next month. Amazon's top-quality Premium Renewed stock has now repriced at Prime Day levels, with up to $220 off new device pricing.

To date, Amazon's top-quality Premium Renewed units have been the best way to grab deals on unlocked iPhone 17 Pro models. Not only do you save hundreds, you also get a 1-year Amazon Renewed warranty and "over 90% original battery life" — whereas non-"premium" Renewed and Refurbished items only come with 90 days of warranty and can't compare on battery life standards.

Now both the 1TB and 512GB iPhone 17 Pro models are back up at up to $220 off — the 512GB version is another $20 less than previously mentioned pricing:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,279 (originally $1,499 new)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,279 (originally $1,499 new)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,279 (originally $1,499 new)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,179 (originally $1,299 new)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,179 (originally $1,299 new)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,179 (originally $1,299 new)

As highlighted in yesterday's Apple Refurbished Store feature, you can grab a perfectly capable iPhone 16 with 1 year of Apple warranty starting from $699, or a 1TB 16 Pro Max for $1,269 — $330 less than the corresponding 17 Pro Max and $130 less than the 512GB 17 Pro.

  • Refurbished iPhone 16 from $699 (up to $330 less than 17 series)
